status: Measured aggregate-key increment; the full sysbench/TPC-C performance goal remains active. See per-case deltas and validation limitations.
change: Cache one existing word-wise fingerprint per pipeline group key. Reuse it for worker routing, map lookup, growth and merging; retain full typed-key equality and charge the extra retained u64. Remove the separate FNV routing loop and temporary integer-routing allocation.
correctness_fix: Restore the compact-bytes tag in the shared collation-aware group-key encoder. NULL and empty strings remain distinct in serial/parallel aggregation and other consumers.
go_source_verification: All three files match the exact running Go binary revision. Go vectorizes key generation, batches accounting and uses murmur3 routing plus its string map. Rust already batches pipeline accounting; this change eliminates repeated byte-wise hashing rather than changing SQL aggregation semantics.

profiles.note: Fingerprint work is inlined into callers; a zero standalone fast_bytes_fingerprint frame is not zero hashing work. Rust fold and Go GetGroupKey/mapper boundaries differ and must not be directly ranked.

validation.profile: Ready scoped checks, release build and lint; one known aggregate plan expectation still fails
validation.red_hash: Derived key hashing wrote 16 bytes even for an empty key; expected one cached 8-byte fingerprint.
validation.red_group: The unchanged serial fold merged NULL with empty string: 7 groups instead of 8. Restore the missing Go compact-bytes type tag in the shared encoder.
validation.collision_test: 402 distinct typed keys forced to one fingerprint, grown and merged three times; all groups, counts and earliest row sequences remain exact.
validation.composite_test: Binary and case-insensitive collation, NULL, empty/NUL/1024-byte strings, signed extremes, composite keys, one-row/partial/full chunks, inline execution and different worker counts.
validation.memory_test: Actual fold charges the retained 8-byte fingerprint once per unique group, for raw integer and encoded keys.

known_failure.detail: Extra Sort(Build) above StreamAgg, identical to the prior independently retained log.

consumer_checks.stream_aggregate: Six ordered groups match Go; EXPLAIN confirms StreamAgg in both Rust binaries.
consumer_checks.window: Candidate partition counts match Go by row id, but ORDER BY id is violated. The control also violates ordering and has wrong NULL/empty partition counts. Ordered equality remains a reported failure.
consumer_checks.source_cause: window::compute_windows reorders rows; driver.rs retains the old order_satisfied scan property and skips the outer Sort. The fix must also audit earlier limit/demand propagation, not only add a late sort.

limitations: Internal group encodings change; no persisted storage key or SQL wire format changes. The extra retained 8 bytes per pipeline group are tracked.
Shared local host and TiKV; only matched within-window comparisons support performance deltas.
Running CPU weights are not blocked time or per-transaction latency; profiled TPS is diagnostic, not acceptance timing.
stream_agg:: and driver::tests::window filters matched zero unit tests. Other scoped suites and live SQL comparisons are reported separately.
The independent point_get estimate mismatch recorded in prepared-range-replay-baseline.json remains open and was not rerun in this increment.
Live window ordering remains incorrect in both control and candidate. Its corrected partition counts are not a claim that the entire window query passes.
TPC-C mixed-write runs remain unapproved and unverified. No fixture reset, commit or push occurred.
Result comparisons and COUNT/SUM checks are not a full-table content hash. No whole-package completion is claimed.

outcome.interpretation: All one/eight-client pairs improve in both workloads. Two of three 32-client pairs regress in each workload. Lower aggregate CPU is confirmed, but this is not a general high-concurrency performance acceptance.
outcome.next: Fix the source-proven stale order/demand contract around window materialization; then continue tracing high-concurrency SQL/TiKV scheduling and batching with matched evidence.
